attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Restates the inference fairly, with 'AI' added from context. It's an unquantified summary judgement with no metric, threshold or period, and the post itself concedes some capacity is coming online.

contract.note: The contract rightly refuses to impose a zero-commissioning reading that the post contradicts, or to invent a delay threshold. Treating the sentence as not scorable is fair.

reviews.rationale: 'All signs point to capacity not coming online' gives no measurable test. A literal zero-capacity reading conflicts with the post's own concession, and any other threshold would be invented. The packet has no evidence items, and none could settle it without a new claim. Not adjudicable, as too vague, not as a broken case.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary of his project survey, endorsed.

semantics.note: Revision 2 keeps 'vast majority', 'in most cases', the 'projects I've found' scope and the concession that some are being completed.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: the projects in the post, a snapshot at publication, roughly two years or more for 'years', and a clear large majority. Campus vs building boundaries still change the count, and no denominator is given.

evidence.note: Edged disclosure dated April 2026: the Atlanta campus had a 27MW building done in 2024 and a 100MW one operating. Shows partial operation for one project, not the share across all projects.
Edged disclosure: the first Aurora facility opened Feb 2025 and the second is due Q2 2027. Bears on the Illinois example's framing, not the aggregate share.

reviews.rationale: The two items show operating buildings on two campuses the post treats as unfinished, which weakens individual examples. But there is no complete roster of the projects he found and no verified May 12 status census, so the vast-majority share can't be confirmed or refuted from the packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Captures the causal core (the purchase worsened margins that were already negative) and drops the Musk descriptions. Naming xAI where the deal was with SpaceX is a minor counterparty slip, not material.

contract.note: Reading 'tanked' as materially worsened and 'deliberately' as knowing acceptance is fair. Zitron gives no accounting basis for the margins, and the result turns on that and on full-year versus realized figures.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure confirms the Colossus 1 agreement (May 6, 2026). It gives no pricing or margin effect.

S-1 filed Oct 26, before the cutoff, unaudited. Revenue and cost of revenue imply about 85% GAAP gross margin for H1 2026, which strongly challenges 'already-negative'. But it covers six realized months, not a full-year projection, and doesn't isolate the deal.

reviews.rationale: e2 points to clearly positive GAAP gross margins in H1 2026, including about two months after the deal, which casts serious doubt on the negative-margin premise. But Zitron's basis is unstated, the contract asks for comparable full-year projections, and nothing isolates the deal's effect or shows knowing acceptance. Not settled under the contract.

attribution.note: Zitron's own blunt conditional statement, endorsed.

semantics.note: Keeps the antecedent (capacity not being brought on) and the firm 'cannot' consequent about contracted revenue. No horizon is given, and the normalisation adds none.

contract.note: Reading the claim as about the cited AWS, Google and Azure contracts and recognized revenue is fair. The antecedent has no capacity threshold or duration, so whether it holds depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Anthropic disclosure of staged Amazon capacity planned for 2026. Neither establishes limited capacity additions nor shows realized contract revenue.

reviews.rationale: Conditional with no deadline. Whether the antecedent (persistently limited capacity) holds is unknown, and no realization, termination or settlement event meets the early-resolution rule. Under the rules it is not scored, so the outcome is unresolved.
